purpose: Render each broad relationship domain as several narrow human-answerable fields instead of one textarea for many distinct questions. Field-level uncertainty is explicit and may trigger clarification text without exposing chart predictions.

RRQ_TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT.title: Relationship timeline & context
RRQ_TRAJECTORY_CONTEXT.intro: Start with what actually happened. Exact dates are not required if you only remember approximate periods.

fields.label: What was the basic timeline? When did it become romantic, roughly how long did that phase last, and what is the relationship now?
fields.placeholder: Example: friends for a year, romantic for about three years, separated in 2019...
fields.clarification_prompt: Describe the different phases separately so we do not average them together.

fields.label: How much were you actually together physically? Include cohabitation and important long-distance or separation periods.
fields.placeholder: Mention what changed when together versus apart, if anything.
fields.clarification_prompt: Which parts apply when together, and which apply when apart?

fields.label: What major transitions or constraints mattered?
fields.placeholder: Breakups/reunions, marriage, other relationships, religion, family, health, money, immigration, language, sexual opportunity, etc. Only include what materially mattered.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate the constraints or transitions and say which relationship phase each affected.

RRQ_LOVE_EROS_DIRECTION.title: Love, attraction & being in love
RRQ_LOVE_EROS_DIRECTION.intro: Keep the two directions separate. Loving someone and being romantically in love with them are not treated as the same thing.

fields.label: You toward them: how physically attracted were you, and were you romantically in love with them?
fields.placeholder: Distinguish attraction from the feeling of being in love.
fields.clarification_prompt: If attraction and being in love differed, describe each separately and when.

fields.label: You toward them: how much did you love/care about them, and how much did you want a lasting partnership or marriage?
fields.placeholder: Love/care can be high even when romantic Eros or long-term fit is not.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate affection/attachment from wanting a durable partnership.

fields.label: Them toward you, as best you could tell: how physically attracted were they, and were they romantically in love with you?
fields.placeholder: Say what you know directly and what is only your inference.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate observed evidence from what you are inferring, and separate attraction from being in love.

fields.label: Them toward you, as best you could tell: how much did they love/care about you, and how much did they want a lasting partnership or marriage?
fields.placeholder: Include direct statements or behavior if useful.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate love/care from commitment or marriage intent.

fields.label: How did any of those feelings change over time, distance, reciprocity, or major relationship events?
fields.placeholder: Only describe changes that were meaningful.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name the phase or condition for each different state.

RRQ_SEXUAL_SYSTEM.title: Sexual system
RRQ_SEXUAL_SYSTEM.intro: Separate general libido, desire for this specific partner, initiation, and how satisfying the actual sexual interaction was.

fields.label: You: what was your general libido like, how much did you specifically want this partner sexually, and how much did you initiate?
fields.placeholder: If general libido and desire for this person differed, say so.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate general libido, partner-specific desire, and actual initiation.

fields.label: Them, as best you could tell: what was their general libido like, how much did they specifically want you, and how much did they initiate?
fields.placeholder: Do not infer libido from low opportunity or prohibition alone.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate what you know about libido/desire from behavior that may have been constrained.

fields.label: When sexual contact happened, how satisfying was it for each of you, and how good was the chemistry as a pair?
fields.placeholder: It is fine if attraction was high but sex was poor, or vice versa.
fields.clarification_prompt: Describe your satisfaction and their satisfaction separately if they differed.

fields.label: Did desire change with familiarity, time apart, reunion, novelty, or other constraints?
fields.placeholder: Mention religion, virginity, health, distance, opportunity, relationship rules, or other factors if relevant.
fields.clarification_prompt: Describe the different conditions separately: what changed, for whom, and under what circumstance?

RRQ_MIND_COMMUNICATION.title: Mind & communication
RRQ_MIND_COMMUNICATION.intro: Reasoning well together is different from being mentally surprised or expanded by somebody.

fields.label: How well could you reason together and understand difficult ideas together?
fields.placeholder: Think about productive disagreement, mutual comprehension, and actually applying ideas—not education level or talkativeness.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate reasoning compatibility from one person's general intellectual ability if those differ.

fields.label: How much did this person surprise you, expand your thinking, or make you see things in genuinely new ways?
fields.placeholder: This can be low even when reasoning compatibility is excellent.
fields.clarification_prompt: What was easy/familiar versus genuinely new or mind-expanding?

fields.label: What were communication quality, communication amount, and shared interests like?
fields.placeholder: Good communication with little to talk about is a valid answer.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate quality of communication, how much you talked, and how much common material you shared.

fields.label: Did they contribute useful knowledge you lacked or stimulate you spiritually/mystically?
fields.placeholder: Useful knowledge, shared spirituality, mystical salience, and intellectual stimulation are separate things.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate useful knowledge, spiritual/mystical resonance, and broader intellectual stimulation.

RRQ_EMOTIONAL_AUTONOMY.title: Emotional climate & autonomy
RRQ_EMOTIONAL_AUTONOMY.intro: We separate intimacy, drama, serious conflict, repair, autonomy, and jealousy instead of calling the relationship simply easy or difficult.

fields.label: How safe was confiding, how psychologically known did you feel, and how readable were you to each other?
fields.placeholder: Someone can be caring but hard to read, or easy to read but unsafe to confide in.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate confiding/safety from how easy each person was to read.

fields.label: How much playful/theatrical drama was there versus genuinely serious conflict, hostility, contempt, coercion, or aggression?
fields.placeholder: Do not count expressive drama as serious conflict unless it actually was hostile/harmful.
fields.clarification_prompt: Describe theatrical/playful episodes separately from serious hostile or harmful conflict.

fields.label: After conflict, how hard was repair, and how emotionally easy or settled did the relationship feel internally?
fields.placeholder: Low visible conflict does not necessarily mean internal ease.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate how quickly you repaired from how easy the relationship felt internally.

fields.label: How much freedom and personal space did each person have, and was there pressure to merge, reassure, attend, or organize life around the relationship?
fields.placeholder: Mention if this changed with cohabitation or greater attachment.
fields.clarification_prompt: Describe each person's autonomy separately and identify when pressure increased or decreased.

fields.label: What happened around sexual jealousy, romantic-priority jealousy, closeness, distance, and other partners?
fields.placeholder: Jealousy about sex can differ from jealousy about love or attention.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate sexual jealousy from jealousy about love/priority, and name any closeness/distance condition that changed it.

RRQ_PRACTICAL_FUTURE.title: Practical future fit
RRQ_PRACTICAL_FUTURE.intro: A relationship can contain strong love and commitment while still having poor practical fit.

fields.label: What kind of long-term relationship did each of you actually want?
fields.placeholder: Marriage/commitment, monogamy or openness, children/family, community/private life, etc.
fields.clarification_prompt: Separate what you wanted from what they wanted.

fields.label: How well did your real-life plans fit on money, work, geography, religion, domestic expectations, lifestyle, family, and community?
fields.placeholder: Only cover domains that materially mattered.
fields.clarification_prompt: Name which life domains fit and which did not rather than averaging them.

fields.label: Which practical strengths or mismatches actually affected whether the relationship could continue?
fields.placeholder: Separate these from love, attraction, or sexual chemistry where possible.
fields.clarification_prompt: If several factors mattered, say which were decisive and which were secondary.
